transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess I'm here because... I just don't really care about anything anymore. Um. I used to do things... art classes, board-game nights. Hiking. Even soccer. But I don't want to get back to the team or... do any of it. I just sit in my room now. It feels like everything is just... slipping away. That's it, really.
Have you ever felt this way for a period of two weeks or longer at any point in your life before this current episode?
I guess... it's been a lot longer than two weeks. Um. It really just became constant around... the summer before last, I think. So it's been about a year and four months now. Just... like this.
During these past sixteen months, have there been any periods of two months or longer where you felt completely back to your normal self and didn't have these symptoms at all?
No. I don't think so. It's just been... the same.

During these past sixteen months, have there been any two-week periods where you felt significantly worse, such as experiencing a deep sense of worthlessness, thoughts of death, or a complete loss of ability to function?
I don't... I don't really know. It all just blends together. I don't think so. It's just been bad the whole time.
Over the past sixteen months, have you noticed any consistent changes in your appetite, such as eating significantly more or less than you used to?

I guess... I don't really eat much. I usually go most of the day without eating. It just... food kind of tastes like cardboard anyway, so I don't bother. Um... my jeans have gotten really loose. I've had to start knotting the waistband just to keep them up.
Over these past sixteen months, have you noticed any consistent changes in how you sleep, such as having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping way more than usual?

I don't really sleep well. I just... I lie there for hours. I have to keep checking the door, and I just listen. And then, when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up way before dawn. I'm usually shaking, and I just... I can't go back to sleep after that.

During these past sixteen months, have there been times where you felt so low or uninterested in things that you also struggled with other issues like feeling extremely guilty, having almost no energy, or feeling like you couldn't focus on anything at all?

I guess... yeah. Mostly I just feel bad about everything. I just... I sit there and keep replaying every little thing I did wrong. In my marriage, and... with my friends. It just doesn't stop. Sometimes I think... I don't know. I just think they'd all be safer, or... less burdened, if I were just gone.

Before that period started sixteen months ago, did you ever have a distinct time in your life—lasting at least two weeks—where you felt this way, or were you consistently your normal self for years before this began?

I don't know... I mean, before the worst of it started, I guess I was still doing okay for a while. I could still cook sometimes... answer texts from friends if I had to. But... um... I was already hearing the voice back then. And... I knew the hallway lights were flashing signals about me. That was going on for weeks before I stopped being able to get out of bed.
During those weeks before you stopped being able to get out of bed, were there times when your mood felt relatively normal, even while you were still hearing the voice and noticing the lights?

Yeah... I guess so. My mood was... fine, mostly. I mean, like I said, I was still cooking... answering texts. But the voice was already there. And... the lights. That was happening for a few weeks while I was still feeling... normal, I guess. Before the bad part started.
During those weeks when you were hearing the voice and noticing the signals in the lights, did you also feel extremely sad, hopeless, or lose interest in all the activities you usually enjoyed?

No, I... I already told you. I was doing okay then. I wasn't really sad yet. I was just... I could still cook, sometimes. Answer texts. But the voice was there. And the lights. That was going on for weeks before the depression... before I couldn't get out of bed.
Are you still hearing that voice and noticing the lights flashing in the hallway even on the rare days when you feel a little bit better or more like yourself?
I don't know... I don't really have days where I feel better. It's just... it's all the same now.
Have the voice and the flashing lights been present continuously every single day during the entire sixteen months you've been feeling this way?

Yeah... pretty much. For most of this past year... it's just been both of them. At the same time. I'll just be... lying in bed, feeling... hopeless, I guess. And she's there. That woman's voice... just telling me I ruined everything. So... yeah. They happen together.
When you hear that woman's voice, does she speak in full, coherent sentences that make logical sense, or is her speech often jumbled, nonsensical, or difficult for you to follow?
She... she makes sense. It's not jumbled. Just... full sentences.
